title: ci: close the number-prefix gap in the arch-review gh allowlist
description:
## Summary
  The Architecture Check workflow pins its allowed `gh` commands to the triggering PR's number, but the bare `<N>:*` entries are string-prefix matches: a pin to PR 123 also allowed `gh pr comment 1234`. Since the agent reads the (untrusted) PR diff, a successful prompt injection could have steered the verdict comment at any same-repo PR whose number string-extends the triggering one — defeating the pin's stated intent.
Each entry now bounds the number with the space-delimited token the prompt already mandates (`--json`, `--name-only`, `--body`), plus an exact match for the bare `gh pr diff <N>`, so the pin is number-exact and the "cannot redirect" comment in the workflow (and in docs/agents/agent-tooling.md) is accurate as written. Impact was low — worst case a bogus bot comment on a neighboring PR — but the fix is one line.
 
  ## Changes
  - `.github/workflows/architecture-check.yml` — bound each `allowedTools` `gh` entry with the trailing token the prompt instructs, and note in the comment why the trailing token is load-bearing

findings.claim: The fix of using exact allowlist entries (mirroring the existing `gh pr diff` entries, e.g. `Bash(gh pr view <N> --json baseRefName,title,body)` plus a fixed `--body-file <path>`) relies on the assumption that the `:*` suffix is a raw string-prefix match; this was not verified against the documentation for the bundled Claude Code version, and if `:*` actually behaves like a word-boundary match (as legacy docs suggest), the old rule was already exact and the new comment describing the fix would be incorrect.

The comment's explanation of how the old `:*` suffix matched may be incorrect: documentation may describe it as equivalent to a word-boundary match (" *") rather than a plain prefix match, in which case the old rule `gh pr comment 123:*` would never have matched `gh pr comment 1234`, meaning the "number-prefix gap" cited as the motivation for this change did not actually exist in the CLI version being used.

If prefix matching is what is intended for these rules, they should instead end with a space-delimited token that cannot be extended, as the comment itself recommends, to prevent unintended flags like --body-file from matching.

Every allowlist rule ends with an open-ended `:*` match, so extra flags can follow the PR number, including gh's inherited `-R/--repo` option. An injected command such as `gh pr comment <N> --body "..." --repo <other-repo>` would still be permitted, letting the token post to a PR in a different repository despite the rule being scoped to a specific PR number.

The gh command allowlist entries for `gh pr view <N> --json:*` and `gh pr comment <N> --body:*` still accept arbitrary trailing arguments, so a `-R`/`--repo` flag could redirect the command to a different repository. This could let a prompt injection in the reviewed PR cause the workflow to read another repository's PR and post its contents publicly, or post the review verdict onto a PR in a different repository, though the actual reach depends on the installed GitHub App's permissions, which the file does not show.

This gap contradicts the workflow's own comment (around lines 126-127) and the statement in docs/agents/agent-tooling.md:63 that a prompt injection cannot redirect these commands to another PR, since the repository can in fact be redirected via an unrestricted trailing flag.

The file most exposed to such exfiltration is `.git/config`, which by default holds the checkout token saved by actions/checkout; the checkout step should set `persist-credentials: false` since the job never needs git credentials.

The comment stating that injection "cannot redirect them at another PR" is inaccurate because that guarantee only holds within the same repository; a redirect to a different repo via `-R` is not prevented.

Making the allowlist entries exact and specific could deny some previously allowed command variants, such as `gh pr diff <N> --color=never`, `gh pr comment <N> -b "..."`, and `gh pr view <N> --comments`; in headless CI this could mean the workflow fails to post a verdict while the run still shows green.

If `:*` is a plain string-prefix match, as the accompanying comment states, then the rule `gh pr comment <N> --body:*` also matches `gh pr comment <N> --body-file <path>`, which would let an injected command post the contents of an arbitrary file on the runner as a public PR comment.

This workflow uses `Bash(gh pr comment:*)`, `gh pr diff:*`, and `gh pr view:*` with no PR-number pin at all, which has the same repo-redirect gap as architecture-check.yml but is broader since it lacks even a number restriction.

The comment's stated reasoning conflicts with the behavior implied elsewhere: if matching is a plain prefix, the `--body:*` rule is too permissive (as noted separately), but if matching is word-bounded, the comment misstates the reason for the change; the actual matching behavior of the bundled CLI should be verified and the comment reworded to match it.

The allowlist rules should place `--repo ${{ github.repository }}` immediately after the PR number in each rule, or use deny rules for `--repo`/`-R` if the tooling supports them, to prevent the repository from being overridden.
